title: Polpo alla griglia
subtitle: Grilled octopus with lemon and olive oil
excerpt: Octopus slow-cooked until tender, then finished on a hot grill until the outside chars and crisps. Dressed with lemon, parsley, and olive oil. A simple, striking dish from the Italian coast.
sourceNotes: Grilled octopus is a standard preparation along the Italian Adriatic and Mediterranean coasts. The technique of braising before grilling is well established across Italian and Greek fish cookery. Cross-referenced with Giorgio Locatelli, Made in Italy (2006).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The braising stage can be done up to a day ahead. Chill the cooked octopus, then grill just before serving.

content.text: Octopus must be cooked twice: first braised slowly in its own juices until tender (about 1 hour), then briefly grilled at high heat until the outside chars. Skip the first stage and the octopus will be chewy and tough. Cleaned octopus is sold fresh and frozen; frozen is sometimes better as the freezing process helps tenderise the flesh.

items.prepNote: cleaned; one large or two medium, tentacles separated

content.text: Put the octopus in a large saucepan with the garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns. Do not add water; the octopus will release its own liquid. Cover and cook over the lowest possible heat for 45 to 60 minutes, until the thickest tentacle is easily pierced with a skewer and the flesh feels tender.
Remove the octopus from the pot and allow to cool for 10 minutes. It can be refrigerated at this point for up to 24 hours.
Heat a griddle pan or outdoor grill to very high. Brush the cooked octopus pieces with olive oil.
Grill for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred in places and slightly crisped. The skin will blister; this is correct.
Transfer to a serving plate. Dress immediately with the lemon juice, extra-virgin olive oil, and parsley. Scatter over chilli flakes if using. Season with sea salt flakes. Serve at once.

items.symptom: The octopus is still tough after 1 hour
items.cause: It needed longer, or the heat was too high during braising
items.fix: Cook for another 20 to 30 minutes. The octopus should feel soft all the way through when pierced.

items.symptom: The octopus sticks to the grill
items.cause: Grill not hot enough or insufficient oil
items.fix: Brush generously with oil and ensure the grill is extremely hot before adding the octopus.

items.symptom: The octopus dried out on the grill
items.fix: The grill stage is brief: 2 to 3 minutes per side. It just needs colour, not further cooking.
Season with sea salt flakes just before serving. Lemon juice and good olive oil are the essential finishers.

content.text: Grilled octopus is eaten along the entire Italian coast, from the markets of Puglia where polpo al cartoccio (octopus in a paper bag) is a street food staple, to Sicilian fish restaurants where it appears as a simple antipasto. The Adriatic version is simpler than the Sicilian one; the Calabrian version is sometimes accompanied by a spiced tomato sauce. The preparation here is the Ligurian-style: let the octopus and the lemon oil speak clearly.
